role.altitude: The history lecturer keeps choosing sources, lecturing, leading discussions and reading the field; retyping syllabus dates, rebuilding the course each year, formatting handouts and scanning journal issues by hand shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using topic alerts and a reference manager
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer whose course set-up takes hours, not days, leaving the time for sources and students.

tasks.short: Choose goals, readings and topics, update the syllabus, write homework assignments, prepare handouts, and set up the course materials in the learning platform.

steps.what: Lecturer decides learning goals, readings and assignment topics for the course
Lecturer updates the syllabi: dates, rooms, deadlines and policies
Lecturer writes homework assignments and essay prompts

loop.input: The topic, the assigned sources and the learning goal.
loop.output: Draft assignment prompts with instructions and the rubric link.
loop.check: Each prompt must name only the assigned sources; the lecturer edits and approves each one.
loop.stop: The lecturer writes the prompt by hand when drafts miss the goal.
loop.why_not_simpler: Prompts change each year to keep answers original.

steps.what: Lecturer prepares handouts with source excerpts, timelines and maps
Lecturer sets up the course materials and deadlines in the learning platform

tasks.design: The syllabus is generated from the learning outcomes, the timetable and the course catalogue, so dates, rooms and deadlines are filled instead of retyped. A drafting step proposes assignment prompts from the topic and the assigned sources, and the lecturer edits each one. Handouts use a template, with citations for source excerpts formatted by the reference manager. The course is copied from last year in the learning platform with dates shifted to the new timetable, instead of rebuilt item by item. Choosing goals and readings stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates were retyped and the course rebuilt each year.
tasks.enabler_now: Syllabus generators, course copy with date shift and drafting of prompts.
tasks.still_hard: New courses without last year's version.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a source that makes students argue.

reach.learn: Whether deadlines in syllabus and platform match.

evidence.claim: AI grading and proctoring duties apply from December 2027; drafting materials is not covered.
Syllabi can be generated from learning outcomes and the timetable, with a model drafting only free text.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing course materials; revising curricula (task 6363) and compiling bibliographies (task 6373) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: timetable and rooms published by the scheduling office before the term.
Choosing goals and readings keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of courses repeated from last year.
research_questions: Is course set-up finished earlier before term?

incremental.description: Lecturer checks shifted dates in the copied course.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: new courses; high: repeat courses with many assignments.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select sources, prepare lecture notes and slides, deliver lectures on topics such as ancient history, postwar civilizations and the history of developing countries, and answer questions.

steps.what: Lecturer selects sources and readings for the lecture
Lecturer prepares lecture notes and slides with images and maps
Lecturer delivers lectures to undergraduate or graduate students on topics such as ancient history and postwar civilizations
Lecturer answers students' questions after the lecture and on the course forum

tasks.design: Slides use the department template, and images and maps come from the library's licensed collections with credit lines filled in, instead of being searched and credited by hand. Selecting sources, lecturing and answering questions stay with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Images were searched and credited one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Licensed image collections with credit data.
tasks.still_hard: Rare sources not in licensed collections.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a story that makes the past feel near.

reach.learn: Whether lecturers use licensed images more.

evidence.claim: Library image collections supply credit data with each image.

assumptions: Boundary: preparing and delivering lectures; preparing course materials (task 6358) and online courses (task 20102) are sibling tasks.
Selecting, lecturing and answering keep their full time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: text-heavy lectures; high: image-heavy lectures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare discussion questions, read students' reading responses, initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions, and note participation.

steps.what: Lecturer prepares discussion questions and source excerpts

loop.input: The assigned readings and the session goal.
loop.output: A list of candidate discussion questions, each tied to a passage.
loop.check: Each question must cite a passage in the assigned readings; the lecturer chooses and rewrites.
loop.stop: The lecturer writes questions by hand when candidates miss the point.

steps.what: Lecturer reads students' reading responses before class
Lecturer initiates, facilitates and moderates the classroom discussions
Lecturer notes participation in the grade book

tasks.design: A drafting step lists candidate discussion questions, each tied to a passage in the assigned readings, and the lecturer chooses and rewrites them. Reading students' responses, moderating the discussion and judging participation stay with the lecturer; no software rates participation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions were written from scratch for each session.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive topics where wording must be careful.
tasks.human_edge: Drawing a quiet student into the discussion.

reach.learn: Whether discussions start from the readings.

evidence.claim: Evaluating learning outcomes with AI is a high-risk use, so participation is judged by the lecturer only.

assumptions: Boundary: classroom discussions; grading class work (task 6357) and grade records (task 6362) are sibling tasks.
s4 is part of maintaining grades and records, which sibling task 6362 covers; its saving is counted there.
Reading responses and moderating keep their full time.
unknowns: Number of discussion sessions per week.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: well-worn readings; high: new readings each week.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Scan new journal issues and books, read current literature, talk with colleagues, participate in professional conferences, and keep notes and references.

steps.what: Lecturer scans new journal issues and book announcements in the field
Lecturer talks with colleagues about developments in the field
Lecturer keeps reading notes and references

tasks.design: Table-of-contents alerts and saved searches on the lecturer's topics deliver new articles and books in one list, instead of the lecturer scanning journal sites one by one. Topic summaries in the literature database help orientation, but the lecturer reads the sources. The reference manager imports citation data by identifier instead of typing. Reading, talking with colleagues and conferences stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Journals were scanned site by site.
tasks.still_hard: Books and journals outside the indexed databases.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which new work changes how the course should be taught.

reach.learn: Whether new work is found sooner.

evidence.claim: A literature database gives topic summaries and foundational papers.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping abreast; research and publishing (task 6365) and reviewing manuscripts (task 20101) are sibling tasks.
Reading, talking and conferences keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of the field covered by indexed databases.
research_questions: Does scanning time fall without missed key works?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: fields with few indexed journals; high: well-indexed fields.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
